clue.text: Ignore the staff set aside during Conference?

indicators.note: during means the set-aside word sits within the fruit word

parts.note: Conference is a variety of pear, hence the question mark
a lay-by is a stretch of road set aside for stopping

explanation.surface: Someone being told to disregard the employees who were sidelined at a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The staff is the musical stave, not employees. Conference is a well-known British pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing without reading written music means paying no attention to the musical stave, the five lines notes are written on.

clue.text: Nominate board for such a dishonest job

definitions.meaning: to ... a candidate is to nominate them
to board a guest is to give them lodging for the night
a crime arranged beforehand, a set-up

explanation.surface: Propose a committee for a crooked piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the first two give the phrasal verb, the third its hyphenated adjective form.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means propose or accommodate; hyphenated it describes something rigged in advance.

clue.text: Foreign workers answer with happy voices

parts.note: feeling up means feeling happy
to air an opinion is to voice it

explanation.surface: Overseas labourers reply with cheerful singing.
explanation.definitionFit: Young people from abroad who live with a family and help with childcare in exchange for board.

clue.text: Save lido swimming, cutting grass, for now?

parts.note: to bank money is to save it

indicators.note: cutting means the jumbled letters cut into the grass word

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of lido moving about

explanation.surface: Rescue the open-air pool by mowing the lawn, for the time being.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' and 'cutting' read as pool and lawn chores. A bank holiday is a British public holiday, when banks shut; the question mark marks the definition as a guess at today.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue offers a public holiday, when banks close, as a possible description of the present day.

clue.text: Partner no longer to make fast ground in SW England

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to moor a boat is to make it fast

explanation.surface: A former spouse hurries to a field in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' means secure, not quick. Exmoor is a national park in Somerset and Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A national park of open upland moor straddling Somerset and Devon.

clue.text: Timber pole in which to stitch rings

indicators.note: in which means the stitching and ring go inside the pole word

parts.note: a rood is an old measure of land, the same as a rod or pole
to sew is to stitch
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wooden post into which you sew loops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pole' is the old unit of measure, not a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark, fragrant hardwood used for fine furniture and instruments.

clue.text: Spotted peeled fruit

indicators.note: peeled means the outer skin, here the first and last letters, is stripped off

parts.note: dappled means marked with spots or patches

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit that was blemished, now with its skin off.
explanation.definitionFit: A common orchard fruit, an example of the general category named.

clue.text: Bore everyone talking

indicators.note: talking means the word for everyone is said aloud and spelt by its sound

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Tedium when all the people are chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' reads as a tedious person; it is the verb make a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: An awl is a pointed tool for piercing holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Left in charge of old architectural feature

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Abandoned under the control of a historic building element.
explanation.definitionFit: A porch of columns supporting a roof at a building's entrance.

clue.text: Continually popular the Queen, and good with soldiers in uniform

indicators.note: in means the queen, good and soldiers go inside the uniform word

parts.note: uniform means even, consistent
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: The monarch, always admired, approves of troops on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' looks like military dress, but it is the adjective meaning even.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or act that never goes out of fashion is called an evergreen.

clue.text: Name of place where boy's crossed small mount

indicators.note: crossed means the boy's name straddles the mount, lying either side of it

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name; the 's stands for has
a pony is a small horse, something one mounts to ride

explanation.surface: A placename marking the spot where a lad rode across a little hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small mount' looks like a hillock, but it is a little horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A toponym is the technical term for a placename, from Greek topos, place.

clue.text: Records reflected desire to spend heavily

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the records abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: LPs are long-playing records
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: Record collection mirrors a craving to go on a spending spree.
explanation.definitionFit: To splurge is to spend extravagantly on a one-off indulgence.

clue.text: Letter from overseas company getting you online backing

indicators.note: backing means the company's initials go in reverse order

parts.note: an ISP, internet service provider, is the firm that connects you to the internet

explanation.surface: A letter arrives from a foreign firm that sets up your internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter from overseas' suggests post from abroad; it is a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is the twenty-third character of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign letter.

clue.text: Taking in success: piece appearing on cover

parts.note: a hood is a head covering
a win is a success
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A tale of achievement where a chessman turns up on a book jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing on' places the success and piece after the cover word in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone in means deceiving them, which is what tricking or duping is.

clue.text: Where Reg is feeling less pressure, behind

parts.note: something that makes you more numb leaves you with less feeling
late means behind time

explanation.surface: A man called Reg feels less stressed at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: Reg is short for a car's registration, the letters and digits on British plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's registration mark is displayed on the plate front and rear.

clue.text: I must bring in Jack briefly for flogging

indicators.note: must bring in means the number word takes the shortened sailor inside it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: jack and salt are both slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone has to fetch a man called Jack for a short whipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' suggests beating; here it is the British slang for selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods offered for sale are being flogged, in the British informal sense of selling.

clue.text: Start when Duke moving key defence installation

parts.note: off means start, as in 'they're off'
as means when

indicators.note: moving means the letters of key are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A duke on the move triggers a crucial defensive system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns KEY into DYKE's last letters YKE. Offa's Dyke is an eighth-century earthwork along the England-Wales border.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa of Mercia built this earthwork bank along the Welsh border as a defensive barrier.

clue.text: Without room, difficulty finding shortcut in theory

parts.note: w/o is the written abbreviation for without
being in a hole means being in difficulty

explanation.surface: Lacking space, a problem arises in finding a quicker route that works on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Physicists theorise that a tunnel through spacetime could give a shortcut between distant points.

clue.text: Christmas cards often have this literary family

definitions.meaning: read as ..., since the red-breasted bird is a familiar card design
The Swiss Family of that surname is the shipwrecked household in Wyss's novel

explanation.surface: Seasonal cards frequently feature a well-known fictional household.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words to see what decorates the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The shipwrecked Swiss Family in Johann Wyss's novel bear this surname.

clue.text: Safety feature benefitting houses I arrange afresh

indicators.note: houses means the word for benefitting contains the other pieces

parts.note: something for you benefits you
to redo is to arrange again

explanation.surface: A safety device that helps homes, which I am reorganising.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-resistant door that slows the spread of flames is a building safety measure.

clue.text: Single keen on encounter

parts.note: a single in cricket is one run
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: An unmarried person is eager for a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' looks like an unattached person; it is one run in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone by chance, unplanned, is to bump into them.

clue.text: One selling wheels by ton — small for time being

indicators.note: wheels means turns round, so the seller's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: small for time means the time letter is replaced by the small letter

explanation.surface: A car salesman paired with a heavyweight, but a smaller one for the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for time being' reads as 'for the time being', but 'time' is a letter swap and 'being' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is an individual creature, so a human individual fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Dickensian villain taking rum on board vessel

indicators.note: on board means the odd word is carried within the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
rum is old slang for strange or queer

explanation.surface: A Dickens bad guy smuggling liquor onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' is the adjective meaning odd, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Wackford Squeers is the cruel schoolmaster of Dotheboys Hall in Nicholas Nickleby.

clue.text: Award winner in hooting competition perhaps hasn't finished

indicators.note: hasn't finished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the best owl would win a hooting contest

explanation.surface: A prize-winner in a hooting contest who didn't complete the course.
explanation.definitionFit: To award something is to confer or present it as an honour.

clue.text: Not over easy being cheerful with team ahead

parts.note: a sunny disposition is a cheerful one
a side is a sports team
up means ahead, as a team leading by a goal is one up

explanation.surface: Things not being straightforward despite a happy mood with the team in front.
explanation.walkthrough: An egg 'over easy' is fried on both sides; one fried only on the bottom is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs fried on one side only, yolk showing, are the alternative to eggs flipped over easy.

clue.text: Good exercise

definitions.meaning: good as a noun, benefit or point, as in 'what's the good of it?'
to exercise a right or skill is to employ it

explanation.surface: A brief verdict that workouts are beneficial.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it means benefit (no good, no point); as a verb it means employ or exercise.

clue.text: Polish nanny remembered after upsetting hosts

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top
hosts means the words of the phrase contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A Polish nanny is recalled after the guests were annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality; it is the abrasive for polishing.
explanation.definitionFit: This abrasive powder of corundum is used on boards and paper to polish and smooth.

clue.text: Foreigners going around Lima in D'Oyly Carte

parts.words: going around Lima in D'Oyly Carte
parts.note: in the name D'Oyly two Ys sit either side of an L; in the NATO alphabet Y is Yankee and L is Lima

explanation.surface: Visitors from abroad touring Peru's capital in a Gilbert and Sullivan opera company.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima is not the city but the NATO code word for L. D'Oyly Carte is the British opera company famous for Gilbert and Sullivan.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees is a name for Americans, who are foreigners from a British point of view.

clue.text: See replay where every second counts

indicators.note: every second means the second, fourth and sixth letters are taken

explanation.surface: Watch the rerun where each moment matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a bishop's diocese, here the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Diocese of Ely, seat of a bishop, is a see in the Church of England.

clue.text: Fluency in speech after gin in swinging bar

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game

indicators.note: in speech means the word for fluency is spoken, and spelt by its sound

parts.note: ease of expression is fluency

explanation.surface: Smooth talk after a drink in a bar for swingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is the snare, not the drink, and 'bar' is a pole rather than a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal pole hung from ropes on which acrobats swing.

clue.text: Stick pants on Elizabeth's head

indicators.note: on means the pants word follows Elizabeth's initial in this across entry
Elizabeth's head is the first letter of the name

parts.note: pants and poxy are both British slang for rubbish, worthless

explanation.surface: Someone wants to put underwear on the Queen's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for poor or rubbish, as is 'poxy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Epoxy resin is a strong adhesive, and as a verb means glue with it.

clue.text: Unfamiliar, neat state

parts.note: something new is not yet familiar
neat is an old word for cattle, and a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: A description of a tidy condition that is strange to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like tidy, but it is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, on the Atlantic coast between New York and Pennsylvania.
